provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Mid-ticket install plus a recurring cleaning plan, so the products lean on plan billing and leaf-season timing. No guard brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Screens, micro-mesh, reverse-curve and foam inserts compared by what they stop: oak leaves, pine needles, maple seeds and shingle grit, and what clogs each one anyway
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers arrive having seen an advert for one guard and want to know if it's worth it for their trees. An honest comparison earns the estimate.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Five-inch versus six-inch K-style, half-round, oversized downspouts, aluminium versus steel versus copper, and a colour chart matched to common trim
pageStructurePlus.why: Size and colour are the two questions asked on every estimate. Answering them on the page shortens the visit and the decision.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Downspout placement, extensions, splash blocks, buried drain lines, water pooling at the foundation and the wet-basement link
pageStructurePlus.why: Many gutter calls start with a wet basement or a washed-out flower bed. Showing the drainage fix turns a cleaning call into an install.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Spring and fall cleaning visits, what each visit covers, downspout flushing, a roof-line check, plan sign-up and how rescheduling around rain works
pageStructurePlus.why: The cleaning plan is how a one-off customer becomes yearly revenue, and the third clogged visit is when they buy guards.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Rotted fascia boards behind sagging gutters, loose hangers, soffit vents, birds and wasps in the eaves, and what changes when old gutters come down
pageStructurePlus.why: Rot is found when the old gutters come off. A page that sets the expectation first stops the quote from feeling like a bait and switch.

designDirections.name: Clear Run

designDirections.name: Clogged to Clear
designDirections.bestFor: Gutter companies with a library of overflowing-versus-new runs and a cleaning plan to sell

designDirections.name: Copper Half-Round
designDirections.bestFor: Copper and half-round gutter specialists working on older homes and custom builds
designDirections.headlineSample: Copper and half-round gutters for {City}'s older homes

openers.line: Your Google listing has a phone number but no website, so someone watching water pour over their gutters can't see what a seamless run from you looks like before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a gutter site behind that button looks like: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website on your listing is your Facebook page. Someone choosing between guard types wants a comparison and an estimate form, and a feed buries both.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest gutter job posted there.
openers.linkLine: A gutter page that compares guards before the estimate: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your gutter site still carries a free-host banner and an old copyright year. When the guards come with a long warranty, people want proof the gutter company will still answer.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a broken form. Note which one.
openers.linkLine: Same gutter company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your gutter site's estimate form was cut off at the side. Most people look up gutter companies from the yard, staring at the overflow.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks: form, menu or call button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your gutter site, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: The only way to get a gutter estimate from you is a call. Plenty of homeowners would rather send the address, the storeys and which side overflows, then hear back.
openers.hook: Check the listing, social pages and any site for a form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: An estimate form that asks for storeys, footage and guards: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your seamless gutter installs on Instagram are tidy, mitred corners and all. They're mixed in with reposts, when a gallery of runs by colour would do the selling.
openers.hook: Pick two installs on their grid you could name by colour and gutter size. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your gutter installs, sorted by colour and style: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews mention gutter guards that actually stayed clear through the fall. That line sells guards, and nobody sees it unless they're already on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about guards, cleanup or a wet basement fixed. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those gutter reviews beside the jobs they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: In a few weeks every gutter in {City} fills with leaves and the cleaning calls pile up at once. The gutter companies with an online sign-up fill their fall list first.
openers.hook: Use this from late August into September. Name the season in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A fall gutter cleaning sign-up, ready before the leaves drop: {demo-link}

openers.line: People notice overflowing gutters during the downpour, usually in the evening. If the gutter company's phone goes to voicemail, they book whoever answers first.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it hits a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A gutter request that works while it's raining: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for gutter installers. Good ladder hands check whether a gutter company looks steady before applying, same as customers.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note, a story or a sign on the truck. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A gutter company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: You cover {City} and the towns around it, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll hang gutters there. 'Gutter guards' plus the town is what they type.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A gutter page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you split gutter guard installs into payments, put it on a page. A whole-house guard job is the number people want broken down before they ask for an estimate.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing in a post, a review or on the truck. Otherwise skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Gutter guard payments explained up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: Gutter work is two storeys up on someone's house. A page that shows your insurance answers the quiet worry about who pays if a gutter crew member falls.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance anywhere, or a state registration if the state requires one. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and warranty on one gutter page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your gutter work comes from roofers and neighbours passing your name on. Even those referrals search for the gutter company before they call.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'our roofer recommended them' or 'did the neighbour's gutters'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a gutter referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is clean gutter work, straight hangers and a good pitch to the downspout. A job like that should lead your page, not sit under the reposts.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished gutter or guard job on their grid and name it: colour, size, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That gutter job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is clean gutter work, good pitch and tidy corners.

I searched for gutter companies in {City} and found {Business Name} on social but no site where someone can compare guards or ask for an estimate. I put together a sample gutter page to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got lost. Here's the sample gutter site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a guard comparison by tree type, an estimate form that asks for storeys and footage, and a fall cleaning plan sign-up. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for gutter companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample gutter site for {Business Name}, with a guard comparison, an estimate form and a cleaning plan sign-up, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many town and guard pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a gutter company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, roughly one whole-house guard job."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. If we start now, the cleaning sign-up is live before the leaves drop."

objections.objection: Most of my gutter work comes from roofers.
objections.handler: "That's a good pipeline. The roofer's customer still searches you before they call, and the site lets you sell guards and cleanings the roofer never mentions."

objections.objection: Gutters are a small job. A website's overkill.
objections.handler: "A single install is small. A street of cleaning plans and guard upgrades isn't. The site is there to sign up the plan, not just book the one job."

objections.objection: Fall is my busy season, I don't have time.
objections.handler: "Then summer is the month to build it. The fall cleaning sign-up fills itself while you're on the ladder."

objections.objection: The guard companies on TV take all the guard jobs.
objections.handler: "They spend on adverts. A local gutter company with an honest guard comparison and a fair price is what people look for after the in-home pitch."

objections.objection: My nephew set up my Facebook page.
objections.handler: "Keep it, it's good for posts. The site is where the estimate form and the cleaning plan live, and the Facebook page links to it."
"{Build Range}. For you, about {Build Price}, because it's a guard comparison, an estimate form and a cleaning sign-up. That's close to one guard job."

email.subject: Gutter site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for gutter companies in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a guard comparison and a cleaning sign-up. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} gutter demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, leaves start dropping in a few weeks and the gutter cleaning calls come all at once. Thought of you.

The gutter site is still here, same price as before. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one whole-house guard job, not to the price of a cleaning visit.
Price the cleaning plan sign-up as its own line; it is the part that keeps paying them every season.
The guard comparison is a separate line from the gallery, and only worth quoting if they install more than one guard type.
Quote the estimate form higher when it collects storeys, linear footage and which sides overflow.
Keep town pages cheap and quick; gutter searches are very local and the jobs are short drives.
Sell the leaf-season pages in summer, when they have time and before every gutter company is booked.

lineItems.item: Guard comparison page by tree type
lineItems.description: Max when it compares several guard types with close-up shots and a short quiz on the trees over the roof.

lineItems.item: Estimate form with storeys and footage fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload of the overflow, a guard yes-or-no question and routing to two estimators.

lineItems.item: Cleaning plan sign-up with recurring billing
lineItems.description: Max when it handles spring and fall visits, card on file, rain rescheduling and a plan-member page.
Max with buried drain line and extension options and a short wet-basement troubleshooting guide.
Max when each town page has its own finished gutter jobs and the common trees on its streets.

lineItems.item: Gutter colour chart on house photos
lineItems.description: Max when it shows every stocked colour against several trim and siding combinations.
Max when the guard comparison, estimate form and cleaning sign-up are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Overflow-to-clear photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Half a day shooting a packed gutter before cleaning, the guard going on, and the clear run after, in rain if we can get it. That's a season of gutter posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the first rainy week after launch.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for gutter and guard jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a new seamless install or guard job goes on your Google profile with the town named, so the map shows a busy gutter company."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each gutter visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After every install or cleaning, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while the gutters are still clear. Those reviews are what the guard buyer reads."

whatElseYouSell.name: Fall cleaning sign-up campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A late-summer push to past customers and neighbourhood groups fills the fall gutter cleaning calendar before the leaves come down."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run in late August.

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck, ladder rack and yard sign artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your ladder rack sits in a driveway all morning. A clean gutter decal and a yard sign with the site on them turn that into estimates from next door."

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour postcards after each guard install
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The houses either side of a guard install share the same trees. A postcard with the finished gutter job and a cleaning offer lands with people who already have the problem."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are guard jobs on the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbourhood group post kit for gutter season
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Ready-made posts and replies for when someone in the neighbourhood group asks who cleans gutters, written so it sounds like you, not an advert."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, before spring or fall cleaning season.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The roofers who hand you gutter jobs need a site with an inspection form. Your gutter page links to theirs, theirs to yours."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Roof and gutter work runs back to back. The gutter owner's introduction gets you past the agency noise roofers hear every week.

withoutAI.route: Exterior painters working the same eaves
withoutAI.whoPays: The painter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Painters pull gutters off to paint the fascia and call you to rehang them. They need a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Painters and gutter crews already share jobs and refer each other at the fascia line.

withoutAI.route: The gutter coil and seamless supplier
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your coil supplier sells to every gutter installer for miles and their site is a price list. Introduce me and I'll build their installer finder."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers have budgets, and their installer list is the next prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The drainage contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a downspout dumps into a soggy yard, someone digs the buried drain. That contractor needs a site, and your drainage page sends them work."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Wet-basement customers need both trades. A two-way referral with a contractor who sells bigger jobs.

withoutAI.route: Chimney sweeps on the same roof line
withoutAI.whoPays: The chimney sweep, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Chimney sweeps are on the roof every fall, same customers, same weeks as your gutter cleanings. They need a booking page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same season, same houses, no overlap in what they sell. Easy referral partners.

withoutAI.route: HOA managers who book community gutter days
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Townhome communities clean gutters on one day for every unit. A sign-up page for the HOA routes the whole street to your gutter crew."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers want one vendor and one page. The gutter client gets a block of addresses in one morning.

withAI.route: Order assistant for the coil supplier
withAI.pitchLine: "Installers type the footage, corners and downspouts and get a coil, hanger and elbow order priced from your yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties installers to one supplier's prices, which is worth more than a rebate to the supplier.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant answers residents' questions about the community gutter cleaning day, takes gate codes and flags units with guards."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers field these questions every season. The gutter client gets cleaner routes.

withAI.route: Wet-basement intake assistant for drainage contractors
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners describe where the water comes in, upload a few shots, and the assistant sorts gutter and downspout problems from grading and drain jobs."
withAI.whyItWorks: Drainage contractors waste visits on jobs that were only a clogged downspout. Those go back to the gutter client.

withAI.pitchLine: "The painter you rehang gutters for loses quotes to slow callbacks. The same follow-up texts as your gutter estimates, set up for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Configuration of something you already built, introduced by a contractor they trust.

withAI.route: Fall booking assistant for chimney sweeps
withAI.pitchLine: "Chimney sweeps get every fall call in the same few weeks as gutter crews. An assistant books the sweep and offers your gutter cleaning on the same visit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both trades fill faster when they share a booking moment.

withAI.pitchLine: "Overhanging branches fill gutters. Tree trimmers get a tool that drafts a pruning quote from yard shots, and they send gutter work back."
withAI.whyItWorks: Tree services sell bigger jobs and pay for faster quoting, and the gutter client introduced them.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for gutter calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every call you miss on the ladder gets a text asking for the address and whether it's a cleaning, a repair or new gutters. You call back with the job sorted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Gutter cleaning reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two days before each gutter cleaning, the customer gets a text to unlock the gate and move the car. Fewer wasted trips on rainy rebook days."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, once the cleaning plan sign-up is live. Needs their schedule and rain policy.

softwareAI.name: Gutter price calculator by footage and storeys
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner enters the house size, storeys and whether they want guards, and sees a gutter price range before you drive out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price per foot by size and material, guard prices and their minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for gutter and guard jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When someone thanks you for guards that held through the fall, a short thank-you naming their gutters and street is waiting for one tap of approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests. Needs ten past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Card-on-file billing for gutter cleaning plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan members are charged after each gutter cleaning is marked done, with a receipt and a shot of the clear gutter. Nobody chases cheques in December."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the plan prices and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Before-and-after report after each cleaning
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew snaps each gutter side before and after, and the customer gets a one-page report with any loose hangers or rot flagged for a quote."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their cleaning checklist and a logo.

softwareAI.name: Guard recommender from the trees over the roof
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads a shot of the trees over the roof and answers three questions, and it suggests which gutter guard fits, from the guards you install."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their guard list and notes on what each handles. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gutter footage estimator from house photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a few shots of the house and an aerial view, and it drafts the gutter footage, corners and downspouts for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the calculator. Needs past jobs with measured footage to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal cleaning route planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every plan member is grouped by street for the spring and fall gutter rounds, so the crew does a whole neighbourhood in a day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once there are enough plan members to route. Needs addresses and crew count.

softwareAI.name: Gutter job tracker from estimate to install
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every gutter estimate, colour choice, deposit and install day on one board instead of the notebook on the dash."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stages and who estimates.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on guards, sizes and cleaning plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do I need six-inch gutters' and 'will guards stop pine needles' at night, from your real notes, and takes a number when it isn't sure."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their guard notes, sizes stocked and plan prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Storm-week overflow check offer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a heavy rain, past gutter customers without guards get a text offering a quick overflow check. That's how guard jobs start."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a customer list marked by guards or no guards.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-estimate notes from the gutter walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house, say the sides, the storeys and the fascia condition, and it drafts the gutter estimate on your template."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Coil and hanger stock tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See how much coil of each colour is on the truck and in the shop, and get a reorder note before the seamless machine runs dry mid-job."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their colour list and a rough count of what's on hand.

softwareAI.name: Plan-member portal for gutter customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members see their next gutter cleaning date, past reports and any repair quotes in one place, and add guards with one tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the cleaning plan and reports running first.

softwareAI.name: Guard upgrade prompt from cleaning notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the crew notes a gutter packed solid for the third visit running, it drafts a guard quote for you to send with that day's report."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after a full year of cleaning notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with pitch and hanger checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Installers check off pitch, hanger spacing, end caps and downspout straps on the phone, with a shot at each step. You see every gutter run without the ladder."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run two crews. Needs their install checklist.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by gutter footage and crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which gutter jobs paid once coil, guards, downspouts and crew hours are counted, and which guard type earns its keep."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs material invoices and crew hours for a season.

softwareAI.name: Content writer for gutter town pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new gutter town page or guard article each month, drafted from your job notes and the trees on those streets, approved by you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for gutter crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for gutter installer and cleaner jobs answer your questions about ladders, heights and a licence to drive the truck, and you only call the fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the gutter calculator for installers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a gutter price calculator for one installer. Every seamless gutter company in the state answers the same phone question all day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first gutter client taught you the pricing logic and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer locator for a gutter guard maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners search for your guard by name and find nobody local. A dealer locator routes them to the gutter installers who carry it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Guard makers sell through installers and need them found. You already know how a gutter installer's site sells.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer map for a coil distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A find-a-gutter-installer map on your site sends homeowners to the installers who buy your coil, and keeps them buying."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on installer loyalty.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Website bundle with every seamless gutter machine sold
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Everyone who buys a seamless gutter machine is starting a business and needs a site. Bundle one with the machine and the dealer looks like a partner."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: New gutter businesses buy a machine before anything else. The dealer meets every one of them first.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member gutter companies a template with a guard comparison and a cleaning plan sign-up as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One deal reaches many gutter owners who already trust the association.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up gutter clients now and then. License my gutter template with the guard pages and cleaning sign-up done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies rarely know the trade. You sell them the finished part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each gutter territory needs town pages and a cleaning sign-up that routes to the right owner. I build it once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Many locations on one template, one contract.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Community gutter-day portal across an HOA portfolio
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community you manage gets one gutter cleaning day page, with unit sign-ups and gate notes, routed to a vetted gutter crew."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms managing many associations buy once and roll out everywhere.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Cleaning-plan module for other exterior cleaners
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Window cleaners and house washers, monthly
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The gutter cleaning plan sign-up and route planner work for any twice-a-year exterior service. Sell it as a module."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Same seasonal-plan problem across several trades, built once.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Leaf-season campaign kit for gutter companies elsewhere
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A ready fall gutter cleaning page, posts and past-customer texts, set up for any gutter company before the leaves drop."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every gutter company needs it the same month. Selling it as a kit avoids custom work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A gutter company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I take one gutter company per city. {City}'s spot is filled; the next town's best gutter crew is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the gutter template, pitch and proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your gutter site and vanished. I can finish it on a gutter template I've already shipped."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy; they need someone who finishes.

upsellLadder.line: "The gutter site and the care plan go on one contract, so changing a guard price or the fall sign-up date is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests after each gutter visit
upsellLadder.trigger: The first gutter install or cleaning finished since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That guard job last week is your first review from the new site. Let's ask every gutter customer the same day."

upsellLadder.offer: Card-on-file billing for gutter cleaning plans
upsellLadder.trigger: The first cleaning plan sign-ups arrive through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "You've got gutter plan members now. Let's charge them automatically after each cleaning instead of invoicing by hand."

upsellLadder.offer: Gutter price calculator by footage and storeys
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of estimate-form data shows the same house sizes and guard questions again and again.
upsellLadder.line: "Most of your gutter estimates are two-storey houses wanting guards. A calculator answers them before you drive out."

upsellLadder.trigger: Neighbourhood groups start asking who cleans gutters, or the fall calendar still has open weeks in late summer.
upsellLadder.line: "People are already asking about fall gutter cleaning in the local groups. Let's fill your calendar before the leaves drop."

upsellLadder.offer: Guard recommender from the trees over the roof
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention answering the same guard question on every call.
upsellLadder.line: "You explain guards for oaks and pines on every gutter call. Let the site do that first."

upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second cleaning crew or the plan list passes what one crew can route by hand.
upsellLadder.line: "Two gutter crews and a long plan list need routes by street. Let's stop driving across town between cleanings."
